checks.name: Recognition
checks.result: 13 synthetic end-to-end recognition tests passed in the final combined run, including independent demo pitch/rhythm ground truth, clefs, keys, accidentals, flags under slurs, beams, dots, rests, resizing and faded JPEG.

checks.name: HTTP and file handling
checks.result: 26 decoder/API tests passed in the final combined run; include real image/PDF decoding, invalid pages, malformed multipart, declared and streamed size bounds, in-memory spooling, and local origin/host policy.

checks.name: Piano and notation editing
checks.result: 95 JavaScript tests passed: 15 piano, 39 notation editing, 17 tempo, and 24 note naming. Independent cases cover all 15 key signatures, written/enharmonic octaves, beat-relative density, transport, and export conversion.

checks.name: Final local checks
checks.result: The complete JavaScript suite passes 95 tests with zero failures. GitHub Actions on feature commit dea0f2a passes the full 39 Python and 95 JavaScript checks in both runs. JavaScript syntax checks pass.

checks.name: PDF decoder integration regression
checks.result: Actual app.decode_score images for all six supplied PDF pages are pixel-identical to the evaluated 2,600-pixel rasters; all 717 MIDI/duration events match the saved evaluation. A regression test fixes the normalized PDF raster dimensions.

checks.name: Launcher
checks.result: The documented Windows .\start.ps1 -NoBrowser -Port 8767 started successfully, returned local health 200, and its task-owned test server was stopped. The main app remains available on 127.0.0.1:8765.

checks.name: Practice defaults and manual choices
checks.result: Actual UI: ordinary 4/4 starts at 72 quarter-note BPM; dense 6/8 starts at 40 dotted-quarter BPM. Manual 65 survives a rhythm edit while the range updates to 48–60; Use suggested applies 56 and resetting notes restores automatic 72. Manual 42 survives PDF page navigation; opening a different score resets its defaults.

checks.name: Scale-aware note names
checks.result: Actual marker and review labels show G-sharp 4 in A major and E-flat 4 in B-flat major; the supplied PDF retains written E-sharp 3. All 15 signatures, naturals, octave boundaries, double accidentals, manual edits, and whole-octave spelling are covered by independent helper tests.

checks.name: Compound export timing
checks.result: A real six-quarter-beat WAV at dotted-quarter 40 lasts 6.16 seconds including release. MIDI encodes 1,000,000 microseconds per quarter, equal to quarter 60. Manual dotted-quarter 45 encodes 888,889 microseconds, equal to quarter 67.5. Browser loop/live tempo/transpose/pause/stop checks pass.

checks.name: Tempo and audition regression checks
checks.result: A stopped seek at beat 7.95 retains its target and 0:07 time at quarter 60 after tempo/transposition changes. Changing transpose during a first-load audition cancels the old pitch and stale highlight. Paused transposition preserves Resume. Desktop/mobile scrollWidth equals clientWidth: 1425/375 pixels respectively.

private_score_summary: The complete six-page supplied PDF was processed locally at a 2,600-pixel long edge: 36 staves and 717 note events in 16.6 seconds total. The independent reviewer visually checked 13 complete staves / 258 events across all six pages, including all 97 notes and rhythms on the last page. All identified flag, sharp, false-rest and key errors were repaired. This does not mean all 717 events were manually verified or guarantee accuracy for arbitrary scores.
audio_summary: The embedded synthetic edited baseline phrase was rendered at 90 quarter-note BPM: stereo 44.1 kHz, 16-bit PCM, 5.8267 seconds, RMS 0.00946 and a strongest FFT bin near 293 Hz (D4). For the new tempo behavior, a six-quarter-beat compound phrase at dotted-quarter 40 rendered 6.16 seconds with matching MIDI quarter 60; dotted-quarter 45 exported MIDI quarter 67.5. Physical speaker output was not instrumented.
browser_summary: Updated real-server checks cover automatic ranges and beat units, remembered manual tempos within and across PDF pages, rhythm edits and Auto reset, key-specific sharp/flat labels, stopped seek clocks, audition cancellation after transposition, live tempo/transpose in a loop, and actual compound MIDI/WAV downloads. The supplied PDF is left loaded on page 1 with automatic quarter-note 72. English is the only implemented language.
limitations: Recognition is an editable heuristic draft for clean, level, printed monophonic treble/bass staves. High reading confidence does not guarantee transcription accuracy.

Handwriting, perspective photos, dense/chordal notation, multiple voices, ties, tuplets, repeats, grace notes and expressive performance are not reliably interpreted. Phrase slurs are ignored; ties require manual consolidation.
Staves play independently; the app does not infer multi-staff instrument parts or join systems. A key signature alone does not determine major versus minor mode.

Uploads are bounded to 25 MiB and raster images to 30 megapixels; processed images have a 2,600-pixel long-edge limit. Local process/browser memory and operating-system swap remain outside application storage controls.
Audio needs a browser gesture and can be suspended by background/locked-device policies. WAV is limited to ten minutes; transport is limited to thirty minutes and 20,000 events.
The server is intended for loopback use. It has no public-hosting authentication or deployment hardening. Initial dependency installation needs internet access.

review.evidence: The previously reviewed bounded local image/PDF decoder and upload paths are unchanged. Tempo choices are browser-local and keyed by page/staff within the active score; a failed new upload preserves the previous score and choices. Lead browser verification retained manual dotted-quarter 42 through PDF page navigation.

Recognition is unchanged from the prior independent review of 36 staves and representative source passages. The refinement uses the recognized meter/key without altering geometry or MIDI. Actual browser checks preserve a written E-sharp 3 from the supplied PDF; no broader recognition accuracy claim is added.

Twenty-four note-name tests independently specify all 15 keys, explicit accidentals, stale/manual metadata, scientific-octave crossings, octave shifts and clamping. Reviewer reran them successfully. New key-aware G-sharp/E-flat labels and preserved E-sharp spelling match browser evidence; naming does not change MIDI or score durations.

Display pulse BPM converts once to quarter BPM for playback, clocks, WAV and MIDI. Reviewer directly inspected actual downloads: dotted-quarter 40 encodes 1,000,000 microseconds/quarter and a six-quarter-beat WAV lasts 6.16 seconds; manual dotted-quarter 45 encodes 888,889. Loop/live tempo/transpose and pause/stop browser checks pass; superseded auditions are canceled.

Lead browser evidence verifies automatic 72 quarter-note BPM and dense 40 dotted-quarter BPM, manual 65 surviving rhythm edits, refreshed 48–60 recommendation, Use suggested at 56, reset automatic 72, and manual 42 across PDF pages. Independent source review confirms applied tempo is distinct from unfinished input and both reported stopped-seek/audition races are repaired.

Reviewer inspected refreshed desktop/mobile screenshots with visible pulse symbols, textual beat/range explanation and Use suggested control. Lead measured no horizontal overflow at 1425/375 pixels. Pitch aria-labels expand accidentals to words; note markers/review preserve written names and keyboard labels follow key context. English only; no formal assistive-technology certification claimed.

Reviewer independently ran the final 41 new helper tests, all passing; the lead's complete JavaScript suite reports 95 passes. Seventeen tempo cases cover beat-relative density, simple/compound factors, invalid input, rounding, engine-compatible bounds and steady staff timing. Both full CI runs on feature commit dea0f2a subsequently passed 39 Python and 95 JavaScript checks.

Focused pure tempo/naming helpers and owning documentation explain practice defaults, beat conversions, enharmonic spelling, and limits. Original independent-review files are preserved. The updated standalone report includes synthetic screenshots, measured export evidence, the refinement assessment, and issue/PR links.
